2456.note: Not assessed to a verdict. Regest 153444 re-read in full (Hungaricana answers curl, 16 Nov 2026): 'Rusztem pasához intézett levél fogalmazványa, mellékelve hozzá két sifrírozott levél, feloldás nélkül', date s.d. '(1549.10.04.)' supplied by the cataloguer; its Konvolut neighbours (153440-153448) are unrelated undated pieces of 1527-1723, so nothing beside it explains the enclosures. All 1549-50 cipher regests of Türkei I Kt. 8-9 carry interlinear or 19th-century decipherments, and several are printed by Nehring (Austro-Turcica 1541-1552, 1995), e.g. Sigismund Augustus's ciphered letters of 10 Oct 1549 to Rüstem Pasha's wife and to Roxelana (43374, 43375, Nehring 377-379, deciphered): the two unnamed enclosures could be copies of such letters. 2522.note: Topelius's own youthful cipher is solved and published: the SLS edition Zacharias Topelius Skrifter (Dagböcker, introduction) says his 'chifferskrift' of Jan 1833 - Feb 1837 is a 27-sign simple substitution (i=j, v=w), deciphered by Vasenius (Zachris Topelius I, p. 382 f.), and the edition prints every ciphered diary passage resolved. The 1832 diary already mentions writing and reading a 'chifferlapp'. The NB 244.182 file 'Chifferskrift 1832' itself was not seen and may be a key sheet or text in that cipher; either way it is a lookup with the published key, not an open cipher.

vetting.closed: Topelius's cipher of 1833-37 is a simple substitution solved by Vasenius and printed resolved in the SLS edition; the 1832 file in Coll. 244.182 is most likely in it (or is its key), so it is a lookup with a published key, not an open cipher.

2581.note: Of the five MHC sheets only 3352 (Refet to Muzaffer, 25 Jun 1921) is ciphertext: about nine lines of four-digit groups in Arabic-Indic numerals on a telegram form, catalogued as not deciphered, nothing written over the groups. 1186 and 3874 are one and the same image, a clear 'suret' (copy) of cipher telegrams of 30-31 Mar 1921, and 1830 and 3284 are clear cover notes, so the lead should be narrowed to MHC 3352.
